summary: Magnum Photos is an international photographic cooperative founded in 1947 by renowned photographers including Robert Capa and Henri Cartier-Bresson. It is owned by its photographer-members who retain copyrights to their work, and it has documented many historical events. The cooperative has faced controversies, including accusations of child abuse in its archive and the suspension of a member, and it has a significant photographic collection donated to the Harry Ransom Center.

claims.text: Magnum Photos was founded in 1947 in Paris.
claims.evidence_quote: It was founded in 1947 in Paris by photographers Robert Capa, David "Chim" Seymour, Maria Eisner, Henri Cartier-Bresson, George Rodger, William Vandivert, and Rita Vandivert.

claims.text: Magnum Photos is a cooperative owned by its photographer-members.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum Photos is an international photographic cooperative owned by its photographer-members

claims.text: Magnum photographers retain all copyrights to their own work.
claims.evidence_quote: Its photographers retain all copyrights to their own work.

claims.text: In 2010, MSD Capital acquired nearly 200,000 original press prints from Magnum, which were donated to the Harry Ransom Center in 2013.
claims.evidence_quote: In 2010, MSD Capital acquired a collection of nearly 200,000 original press prints of images taken by Magnum photographers, which in 2013 it donated to the Harry Ransom Center.

claims.text: Rita Vandivert was the first president of Magnum Photos.
claims.evidence_quote: Rita Vandivert was the cooperative's first president and head of the New York office

claims.text: Magnum's membership system includes Nominee, Associate, and Full Member stages.
claims.evidence_quote: in 1955 a three-stage membership system was set up that continues to this day

claims.text: Magnum's digital archive contains more than 1 million images.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum Photos' digital archive constitutes more than 1 million images

claims.text: In August 2020, Magnum's website was taken offline due to concerns about photographs of children with nudity and potential child sexual abuse.
claims.evidence_quote: In August 2020, the Magnum website was taken offline after issues were raised by the Fstoppers photography website and amplified on social media

claims.text: David Alan Harvey was suspended for a year following sexual misconduct allegations.
claims.evidence_quote: Harvey was later suspended for a year following a formal investigation into sexual misconduct allegations against him.

claims.text: The name 'Magnum' was chosen because it suggests greatness in Latin, toughness in gun connotation, and celebration in champagne mode.
claims.evidence_quote: It was . . . presumably agreed by those present [at the first meeting] that Magnum was a fine new name for such a bold new venture, indicative as it was of greatness in its literal Latin translation, toughness in its gun connotation and celebration in its champagne mode.
